newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq lambasts France for refusing Uday treatment.
newsitem.headline: Iraq lambasts France for refusing Uday treatment.

text.p: Iraq's ruling party newspaper said on Friday that France would be committing a grave error if it went ahead with its decision not to allow medical treatment on its territory for President Saddam Hussein's eldest son Uday.
"If the news is true we will find that the French government would be committing a big mistake if it did so," the Baath party newspaper Thawra said in a front-page editorial.

France said on Sunday that Uday, who was wounded in an assassination attempt in Baghdad last month, would not be given medical treatment on its soil. A French foreign ministry spokesman did not give a reason for France's decision.
"The rejection of treating a patient entails the taking of a stand...this may cause harm to it (France)," Thawra said.
It said France took its "wrong decision" because it feared reaction from the United States and Britain.

It called on France to review its policy before "losing many opportunities in the Arab world, most important of them in Iraq." The newspaper also lambasted France for its colonial past and what it described as "atrocities" it committed against the Arab nation.

Uday told a visiting Palestinian cleric from his hospital bed early this month that four bullets were still lodged in his body following the attempt on his life when unidentified gunmen opened fire on his car.

Thawra's remarks came as Iraqi Deputy Prime Minister Tareq Aziz praised France during his latest visit to Paris for breaking ranks with the United States and Britain in policing a no-fly zone in northern Iraq.
Aziz said during the visit that France had the largest share of contracts under Iraq's oil deal with the United Nations allowing Baghdad partial exports worth $2 billion in six months.

But France told Iraq the international embargo in force since 1990 for its invasion of Kuwait could only be lifted if it complied with U.N. Security Council resolutions related to the 1991 Gulf war which ousted its troops from the Gulf state.
France was Iraq's main Western arms supplier before the Gulf War. Baghdad owes Paris more than $5 billion and the French are keen to restore economic ties once the embargo is over.
